Self-test — the proof

A coherent drive would turn a qubit clean from |0⟩ to |1⟩ — a full flip. But peek at it along the same axis, again and again, and you keep catching it still at |0⟩: each look collapses the tiny drift back to the pole. Peek often enough and the flip is frozen out — P(stay) = cos2N(π/2N) → 1. A watched pot never boils. Crank N below and feel the coin pin to the pole.

Press Drive the flip. With N peeks the drive is chopped into N nudges, each yanked back to the pole.

Low N (1–16): count the per-peek yank-flashes. High N (32–128): they blur into a frozen shimmer and the drift-wedge becomes a sliver. The drive is unchanged — only the watching grows. Hit rotate, don't collapse to take the looking away: the same chopped drive sails clean to |1⟩.

Scope & honesty. An idealized two-level qubit under a perfect coherent drive, with ideal, instantaneous, perfect projective peeks along ẑ and no decoherence between them — the textbook Zeno limit measured by Itano, Heinzen, Bollinger & Wineland (Phys. Rev. A 41, 2295, 1990). P(stay) is computed two independent ways in the sole core and agrees to machine ε. Honest edge: N=0 and N=1 both give a full flip — one peek taken after the whole turn still finds it flipped; the freeze is an N ≥ 2 story, and it needs peeks that truly collapse (real apparatus leaks, and for some baths frequent looking can speed decay — the anti-Zeno effect).
